IncidentBot: Pager: runtime-memory-surge on runtime-prod-gpu-7 (sev2) — 4455551212
Alex: Acked, I'm taking lead. Assigning Maya for on-call handoff.
Maya (oncall): Oncall here, digging in. Initial customer impact: two customers seeing 504s on generation endpoints.
Jess: Seen increased GPU eviction counts across pool 'infer-prod-a'. Sending quick telemetry.
Dan: Can you post free mem + eviction snippet?
Jess: ```gpu0 free_mb=120 eviction_count=23 kv_cache_used_mb=3200 kv_cache_max_mb=4096 page_faults=142```
Alex: Looks like kv-cache growth nearing limit -> paging. Hypothesis H1: KV cache retention causing fragmentation under high batch sizes.
Elio: H2: abrupt batch-size growth from a rollout caused extra KV pressure. Any traffic changes?
Maya (oncall): We saw a spike at 09:12 UTC after a client surge. Rolling 99th latency jumped. Putting mitigations: lower default batch size for heavy models to 4.
Alex: Patch command for canary: `/deploy infra:scale-model --pool infer-prod-a --batch-size=4 --canary=2`
Jess: Canary done, two nodes now at batch=4. Telemetry: eviction_count down to 6 on canaries after 90s.
Dan: On larger pool, temporarily disable prefix/KV caching for model-x to reduce KV memory pressure. Command: `redwood runtime config set model-x kv_cache.enabled=false --pool infer-prod-a`
Maya (oncall): Applied to high-traffic nodes. Routing update: critical customers A and B moved to dedicated fallback pool 'infer-dedicated-1'.
Elio: Captured logs and timeline. Uploading consolidated logs: gs://redwood-incident-logs/4455551212/ (trace.json, eviction_snaps/, perf_charts/).
Alex: Need a 5-min contiguous memory trace and per-request KV size: `curl -sS localhost:9090/telemetry?trace=mem,kv&dur=300 > trace.json`
Jess: Pushed trace.json to GCS. Early look: avg KV per request increased from 28MB -> 54MB during spike.
Maya (oncall): Customer impact: two customers saw ~3-4% request error increase for ~12 minutes. CS notified and ticket INC-4455 opened.
Dan: Long-term action ideas: 1) soft-limits on kv-cache per-model; 2) autoshrink policy when page_faults > threshold; 3) fragmentation-aware GPU allocator.
Elio: Recording hypotheses: H1 (kv retention + large batches => fragmentation), H2 (client traffic burst + larger prompt shapes => sudden KV growth), H3 (kernel-level GPU allocator fragmentation).
Alex: Next steps: create playbook for lowering batch size + disabling kv cache. Assign follow-ups: Jess -> timeline + charts; Dan -> allocator/patch feasibility; Elio -> customer impact summary. Postmortem draft due EOD.
Maya (oncall): Removing active pager, incident marked mitigated at 4455551290. Will update the timeline in postmortem channel.
IncidentBot: Incident 4455551212 severity downgraded to p2, mitigation actions recorded.
